To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ethanol withdrawal in female rats, as measured by loss-of-righting reflex (LORR) duration, is associated with increased Arc labeling in the lateral hypothalamus, medial amygdala, paraventricular nucleus, and ventrolateral preoptic area (VLPO) of the hypothalamus.

the loss-of-righting reflex (LORR) induced by ethanol withdrawal is a reliable model of ethanol dependence and withdrawal and that the LORR induced by withdrawal is associated with alterations in the number and distribution of cells that are immunoreactive to Arc.

the effects of ethanol withdrawal in rats on the loss of righting response are associated with altered expression of the immediate-early gene Arc in brain regions that are known to be involved in ethanol withdrawal and that the magnitude of these effects are influenced by the sex of the rats.
